quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Whereas conventional wisdom holds that establishing a single consistent bedtime every night, regardless of the day's events, is essential for good sleep hygiene, sleep researchers studying shift workers and parents of young children have increasingly emphasized a related but distinct concept: maintaining a consistent pre-sleep routine, such as the same sequence of dimming lights and avoiding screens, may matter more for sleep quality than the exact clock time itself, since the routine signals the body to prepare for rest regardless of when it occurs. This distinction has offered some relief to people whose schedules genuinely cannot accommodate a fixed bedtime.
options: A Fixed Clock Time Confirmed as Essential for Good Sleep
Pre-Sleep Routines Found to Have No Effect on Sleep Quality
Shift Workers Found to Need No Sleep Routine at All
Routine, Not Exact Bedtime, Found to Matter Most for Sleep
quests.correctAnswer: Routine, Not Exact Bedtime, Found to Matter Most for Sleep
quests.hint: Think about the conventional advice regarding bedtime versus the related but different idea researchers emphasize about routines.
quests.explanation: The passage distinguishes between a fixed clock time and a consistent routine, suggesting the routine itself matters more than the exact hour, so the summary should capture that distinction rather than confirm the importance of a fixed bedtime.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Although group projects have traditionally been assigned with the assumption that working alongside peers naturally teaches collaboration skills through repeated practice, organizational psychologists studying teamwork point out that simply being placed in a group does not guarantee that students learn how to navigate disagreement, delegate fairly, or manage a free-riding member, skills that require explicit instruction and reflection rather than mere exposure. Schools that paired group projects with structured reflection exercises about the collaboration process itself, not just the project content, found students reported more transferable teamwork skills than students who completed similar group projects without that added reflection.
options: Structured Reflection, Not Mere Group Exposure, Building Real Teamwork Skills
Simple Group Exposure Confirmed Sufficient to Teach Collaboration
Structured Reflection Found to Reduce Transferable Teamwork Skills
Students Found to Naturally Learn Delegation Without Any Instruction
quests.correctAnswer: Structured Reflection, Not Mere Group Exposure, Building Real Teamwork Skills
quests.hint: Think about what schools traditionally assumed group projects would automatically teach, and what additional element the research found was actually necessary.
quests.explanation: The passage challenges the assumption that mere group participation teaches collaboration, showing that explicit reflection on the process was necessary for real skill transfer, so the summary should capture that added requirement rather than confirm that exposure alone suffices.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Whereas annual employee surveys have traditionally been the primary tool organizations use to gauge workplace morale, providing a once-yearly snapshot that managers then spend months interpreting and acting upon, some companies have shifted toward brief, frequent pulse surveys sent weekly or biweekly, sacrificing depth for the ability to detect morale shifts in near real time. Managers using pulse survey data reported catching emerging problems, such as dissatisfaction following a policy change, within days rather than discovering the issue months later in the next annual survey, by which point the problem had often already caused measurable turnover.
options: Annual Surveys Confirmed to Catch Problems Faster Than Pulse Surveys
Pulse Surveys Found to Provide No Useful Information to Managers
Turnover Found to Decrease Regardless of Survey Frequency
Frequent Pulse Surveys Catching Morale Problems Annual Surveys Missed
quests.correctAnswer: Frequent Pulse Surveys Catching Morale Problems Annual Surveys Missed
quests.hint: Think about the trade-off between the depth of an annual survey and the speed of a frequent pulse survey, and which one helped managers catch problems sooner.
quests.explanation: The passage shows that trading survey depth for frequency allowed managers to detect and address problems much faster than the traditional annual approach, so the summary should capture that speed advantage rather than describe annual surveys as equally effective.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Although travel rewards credit card programs have traditionally marketed themselves primarily through the number of points earned per dollar spent, financial analysts examining redemption data point out that the actual value of those points varies dramatically depending on how they are redeemed, with some redemption options worth several times more per point than others offered by the very same program. A consumer earning what appears to be a generous points rate could therefore end up with rewards worth considerably less in practice than a consumer earning a lower advertised rate but redeeming more strategically, complicating any simple comparison between competing card offers based on earning rates alone.
options: Earning Rate Confirmed as the Only Factor That Matters
Redemption Strategy, Not Earning Rate, Determining Real Rewards Value
All Redemption Options Found to Offer Identical Value
Consumers Found to Always Redeem Points at Maximum Value
quests.correctAnswer: Redemption Strategy, Not Earning Rate, Determining Real Rewards Value
quests.hint: Think about what travel reward programs typically advertise versus what financial analysts say actually determines how valuable the rewards turn out to be.
quests.explanation: The passage shows that advertised earning rates alone do not determine the actual value of rewards, since redemption choices create large value differences, so the summary should capture that more complete picture rather than focus only on earning rate.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Whereas grief counseling has traditionally encouraged grieving family members to follow a roughly predictable sequence of emotional stages on the path toward acceptance, more recent psychological research suggests that grief rarely unfolds in any consistent linear order, with individuals often cycling unpredictably between emotions or skipping stages entirely depending on their relationship with the deceased and their own coping style. Counselors who have moved away from presenting a fixed-stage model report that clients seem to feel less pressure to grieve 'correctly,' since they are no longer measuring their own experience against an expected sequence that research suggests was never as universal as once believed.
options: Fixed-Stage Grief Models Confirmed as Universally Accurate
Clients Found to Prefer Following a Strict, Predictable Sequence
Moving Away from Fixed Grief Stages Easing Pressure on Clients
Research Found to Fully Support the Traditional Stage Model
quests.correctAnswer: Moving Away from Fixed Grief Stages Easing Pressure on Clients
quests.hint: Think about the traditional model of grief counseling and what effect abandoning that fixed sequence had on how clients experienced their own grief.
quests.explanation: The passage challenges the traditional fixed-stage model of grief, showing that research does not support it as universal, and that moving away from it reduced pressure on grieving clients, so the summary should capture that shift and its benefit.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Although warranty extensions have traditionally been priced by retailers as a relatively small add-on cost compared to the price of the product itself, an analysis of the actual likelihood that a given product category will need a covered repair within the warranty period reveals that extended warranty profit margins for retailers are often extraordinarily high relative to the genuine risk being insured against, since most products in many categories rarely fail within the covered window. Consumer advocates argue that this gap between perceived and actual risk is precisely what makes extended warranties profitable enough for retailers to promote them so persistently at checkout.
options: A Gap Between Perceived and Actual Risk Driving Warranty Profits
Extended Warranties Confirmed to Reflect Genuine Repair Risk Accurately
Most Products Found to Frequently Fail Within the Warranty Period
Retailers Found to Earn Little Profit from Extended Warranties
quests.correctAnswer: A Gap Between Perceived and Actual Risk Driving Warranty Profits
quests.hint: Think about how likely products actually are to need repairs within the warranty period compared to how warranties are priced and promoted.
quests.explanation: The passage shows that the profitability of extended warranties comes from a mismatch between actual low failure rates and how the product is priced and marketed, so the summary should capture that gap rather than assume warranty pricing reflects real risk.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Whereas food expiration dates have traditionally been interpreted by most consumers as a firm safety deadline after which a product becomes unsafe to eat, food scientists point out that most printed dates actually reflect a manufacturer's estimate of peak quality rather than a strict safety cutoff, meaning many products remain perfectly safe to consume well after the printed date, provided they have been stored properly. Studies estimating household food waste have found that confusion over this distinction contributes to a substantial portion of edible food being discarded prematurely, prompting some manufacturers to begin replacing ambiguous date labels with clearer language distinguishing 'best by' quality dates from genuine safety-relevant dates.
options: Expiration Dates Confirmed to Indicate a Strict Safety Deadline
Clearer Labels Found to Increase Confusion About Food Safety
Misunderstood Expiration Dates Driving Avoidable Household Food Waste
Food Waste Found to Be Unrelated to Date Label Confusion
quests.correctAnswer: Misunderstood Expiration Dates Driving Avoidable Household Food Waste
quests.hint: Think about what consumers typically believe expiration dates mean versus what food scientists say the dates actually represent, and what consequence that confusion has caused.
quests.explanation: The passage shows that a common misunderstanding about date labels, mistaking quality estimates for safety deadlines, has contributed to unnecessary food waste, so the summary should capture that connection rather than confirm dates as strict safety cutoffs.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Although facial recognition technology has traditionally been evaluated primarily on its overall accuracy rate across a full dataset, civil rights researchers analyzing performance broken down by demographic subgroup have found that several widely deployed systems show significantly higher error rates for certain skin tones and genders than the overall accuracy figure would suggest, since errors concentrated within particular subgroups can be mathematically averaged out by high accuracy among other subgroups within the same overall statistic. This finding has led some jurisdictions to require subgroup-specific accuracy reporting before approving facial recognition systems for public use, rather than relying on a single overall accuracy number.
options: Subgroup Analysis Revealing Bias Hidden Within Overall Accuracy Rates
Overall Accuracy Rates Confirmed to Reflect Performance Across All Groups Equally
Subgroup-Specific Errors Found to Have No Effect on Overall Statistics
Jurisdictions Found to Reject Subgroup Reporting Requirements
quests.correctAnswer: Subgroup Analysis Revealing Bias Hidden Within Overall Accuracy Rates
quests.hint: Think about what an overall accuracy statistic can hide when error rates differ significantly between specific subgroups within the larger dataset.
quests.explanation: The passage shows that a single overall accuracy figure can mask significant disparities between subgroups, prompting new reporting requirements, so the summary should capture that hidden bias and its policy consequence rather than confirm the reliability of overall statistics.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Whereas annual physical examinations have traditionally been recommended for all healthy adults regardless of individual risk factors, on the theory that regular general checkups catch problems before symptoms appear, several large studies comparing health outcomes between adults who received annual physicals and those who did not found no significant difference in long-term mortality or major illness rates between the two groups, particularly among adults without specific risk factors warranting closer monitoring. Some health systems have responded by shifting resources toward risk-based screening tailored to individual factors like family history, rather than universal annual exams for every healthy adult.
options: Annual Physicals Confirmed to Significantly Reduce Mortality
Studies Finding No Outcome Benefit from Universal Annual Physicals
Risk-Based Screening Found to Produce Worse Outcomes Than Universal Exams
Health Systems Found to Increase Universal Annual Exams After the Studies
quests.correctAnswer: Studies Finding No Outcome Benefit from Universal Annual Physicals
quests.hint: Think about the traditional reasoning behind recommending annual physicals for everyone and what the large studies actually found when comparing outcomes between those who had them and those who did not.
quests.explanation: The passage challenges the assumption that universal annual physicals improve outcomes, showing no significant difference in major studies, and describes a shift toward individualized risk-based screening instead, so the summary should capture that finding and resulting policy shift.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Although streaming services have traditionally measured a show's success primarily through total viewership numbers within the first month of release, some platforms have begun placing additional weight on a metric tracking how often viewers actively discuss a show on social media relative to how many people have actually watched it, reasoning that a show generating disproportionate conversation relative to its viewership may indicate a passionate niche audience capable of driving longer-term subscriber retention even without massive initial viewing numbers. Shows identified through this conversation-to-viewership ratio have in several cases received renewal despite modest viewership that would have led to cancellation under the traditional viewership-only model.
options: Total Viewership Confirmed as the Only Metric That Matters
Shows with High Conversation Ratios Found to Always Get Canceled
Social Media Discussion Found to Have No Connection to Renewal Decisions
A Conversation-to-Viewership Ratio Saving Shows from Viewership-Based Cancellation
quests.correctAnswer: A Conversation-to-Viewership Ratio Saving Shows from Viewership-Based Cancellation
quests.hint: Think about the traditional metric platforms used to decide renewals and the new metric that allowed some lower-viewership shows to survive anyway.
quests.explanation: The passage shows that a new engagement-based metric allowed shows with passionate niche audiences to be renewed despite modest traditional viewership numbers, so the summary should capture that shift in evaluation criteria and its real effect on renewal decisions.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Whereas product recall notices have traditionally been distributed primarily through mailed letters to registered product owners, a method that depends heavily on accurate, up-to-date mailing records that companies often lack for products purchased secondhand or registered years earlier, manufacturers have increasingly begun supplementing mailed notices with targeted social media advertising and retailer point-of-sale alerts triggered at checkout when a customer purchases a related product. Analysis of recall response rates found that supplementing mail with these additional channels measurably increased the percentage of affected products that were actually returned or repaired, particularly for products originally purchased more than five years before the recall was issued.
options: Mailed Letters Confirmed as the Most Effective Recall Method
Additional Channels Found to Decrease Recall Response Rates
Supplemental Channels Improving Recall Response for Older Products
Response Rates Found to Be Unaffected by Notification Method
quests.correctAnswer: Supplemental Channels Improving Recall Response for Older Products
quests.hint: Think about the limitation of relying only on mailed notices and what happened to recall response rates once companies added other communication channels.
quests.explanation: The passage identifies a specific weakness in mail-only recall notices, especially for older or secondhand products, and shows that adding other channels improved response rates, so the summary should capture that improvement rather than confirm mail alone as sufficient.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Although many people assume that the most effective way to break an unwanted habit is through sheer willpower and conscious resistance whenever the urge arises, behavioral researchers studying habit formation note that habits are largely triggered automatically by environmental cues, meaning that simply removing or altering the trigger, such as not keeping snack food visible on a counter, often proves more reliably effective than relying on willpower to resist a cue that remains constantly present. Participants who redesigned their environment to remove specific triggers reported significantly fewer lapses than participants who relied primarily on willpower while keeping their environment unchanged.
options: Willpower Alone Confirmed as the Most Reliable Method
Environmental Triggers Found to Have No Influence on Habits
Participants Who Changed Their Environment Reporting More Lapses
Removing Triggers Outperforming Willpower Alone in Breaking Habits
quests.correctAnswer: Removing Triggers Outperforming Willpower Alone in Breaking Habits
quests.hint: Think about the common belief that willpower alone breaks habits, and consider what the research found about removing the environmental triggers that set habits in motion.
quests.explanation: The passage challenges the assumption that willpower alone is the most effective method, showing that altering environmental triggers produced more reliable results, so the summary should capture that comparative finding rather than confirm willpower as sufficient on its own.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Whereas foreign language education in many school systems has traditionally begun in early adolescence, based partly on logistical convenience rather than developmental research, studies of language acquisition suggest that while younger children do not necessarily learn grammar rules faster than adolescents, they often develop more native-sounding pronunciation due to greater neurological flexibility in distinguishing unfamiliar sounds at a younger age. This has led some education researchers to argue that the ideal timing for language instruction may depend heavily on which specific skill, pronunciation versus grammatical complexity, a program prioritizes, rather than there being one universally ideal starting age for all aspects of language learning.
options: Ideal Language-Learning Age Depending on Which Skill Is Prioritized
Younger Children Confirmed to Learn Grammar Faster Than Adolescents
One Universal Starting Age Confirmed as Ideal for All Skills
Pronunciation Found to Improve Equally Regardless of Starting Age
quests.correctAnswer: Ideal Language-Learning Age Depending on Which Skill Is Prioritized
quests.hint: Think about the two different language skills the passage compares and why the ideal starting age might differ depending on which skill matters most to a program.
quests.explanation: The passage shows that the often-assumed advantage of starting young applies specifically to pronunciation rather than grammar, suggesting no single ideal age exists for all skills, so the summary should capture that skill-dependent nuance.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Although employee handbooks have traditionally been written as dense, comprehensive documents covering every conceivable policy in formal legal language, intended to protect the company from liability by documenting every rule explicitly, usability studies of new employee onboarding found that most new hires retained only a small fraction of handbook content regardless of how thoroughly it was written, since the sheer volume and density of information at the start of a new job overwhelmed most readers' capacity to absorb and remember it. Companies that supplemented dense handbooks with short, separated micro-trainings on individual policies delivered over the following weeks found measurably better policy retention than companies relying on the handbook alone.
options: Dense Handbooks Alone Confirmed to Maximize Policy Retention
Spaced Micro-Trainings Improving Policy Retention Beyond Dense Handbooks Alone
New Hires Found to Retain Most Handbook Content Regardless of Format
Micro-Trainings Found to Reduce Overall Policy Retention
quests.correctAnswer: Spaced Micro-Trainings Improving Policy Retention Beyond Dense Handbooks Alone
quests.hint: Think about why a comprehensive handbook alone failed to ensure new hires remembered policies, and what additional approach actually improved retention.
quests.explanation: The passage shows that information overload undermined the traditional handbook approach, and that spreading instruction out over time improved retention measurably, so the summary should capture that comparative improvement rather than confirm the handbook alone as sufficient.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Whereas airport security procedures have traditionally applied the same screening process uniformly to every passenger regardless of individual travel history or risk profile, several countries have implemented trusted traveler programs that allow pre-vetted, low-risk frequent travelers to use expedited screening lanes in exchange for a background check and application fee completed in advance. Analyses of program data show that resources freed up by moving low-risk travelers through expedited lanes have allowed security staff to dedicate more thorough attention to the smaller number of travelers screened through standard lanes, a reallocation some security researchers argue has improved overall screening effectiveness rather than simply offering a convenience perk to frequent travelers.
options: Uniform Screening Confirmed to Be More Effective Than Tiered Screening
Trusted Traveler Programs Found to Be Purely a Convenience Perk
Expedited Lanes Freeing Resources for More Thorough Standard Screening
Standard Lane Screening Found to Receive Less Attention After the Change
quests.correctAnswer: Expedited Lanes Freeing Resources for More Thorough Standard Screening
quests.hint: Think about how moving low-risk travelers to expedited lanes might affect the resources available for screening everyone else, not just the convenience for those travelers.
quests.explanation: The passage argues that the program's benefit extends beyond convenience, since it freed up resources that improved screening for remaining travelers, so the summary should capture that broader security argument rather than describe the program as merely a perk.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Although estate planning has traditionally focused primarily on the equal division of financial assets among children, family mediators increasingly note that disputes after a parent's death often center less on the actual monetary value received and more on perceived fairness regarding sentimental items, such as who receives a particular piece of furniture or jewelry, regardless of its appraised worth. Families who addressed the distribution of sentimental items explicitly and separately from the financial estate plan, sometimes through a written list specifying recipients for specific meaningful objects, reported significantly fewer conflicts among siblings after a parent's passing than families who left sentimental items to be sorted out informally alongside the financial estate.
options: Separately Planning Sentimental Items Reducing Sibling Conflict After Death
Financial Asset Division Confirmed as the Main Source of Disputes
Sentimental Items Found to Cause No Conflict Among Siblings
Informal Sorting of Sentimental Items Found to Reduce Conflict Most
quests.correctAnswer: Separately Planning Sentimental Items Reducing Sibling Conflict After Death
quests.hint: Think about what family mediators say disputes are actually about, beyond just money, and what specific planning step reduced conflict over those other items.
quests.explanation: The passage shows that explicit planning for sentimental items, separate from financial assets, reduced family conflict more than leaving such items to be sorted informally, so the summary should capture that specific finding rather than focus only on financial division.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Whereas furniture retailers have traditionally relied on in-store displays and printed catalogs to help customers visualize how a piece might look in their own home, augmented reality apps that overlay a virtual, to-scale image of furniture onto a live camera view of a customer's actual room have begun reducing a specific category of returns: items returned not because of any defect or quality issue, but simply because the piece looked different, often larger or smaller than expected, once placed in the customer's actual space. Retailers offering this technology report that overall return rates for furniture have dropped meaningfully since adoption, concentrated specifically among this size-and-fit category of returns.
options: Printed Catalogs Confirmed to Reduce Returns More Effectively
AR Visualization Cutting Furniture Returns Caused by Size Mismatch
AR Technology Found to Increase Size-Related Furniture Returns
Furniture Return Rates Found to Be Unrelated to Visualization Tools
quests.correctAnswer: AR Visualization Cutting Furniture Returns Caused by Size Mismatch
quests.hint: Think about the specific type of return problem the passage describes and how the augmented reality technology addressed that particular issue.
quests.explanation: The passage identifies a specific category of return, size mismatch, and shows that AR visualization reduced that particular problem, so the summary should capture that targeted improvement rather than describe returns in general.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Although plant-based meat alternatives have traditionally been marketed primarily to vegetarians and vegans seeking meat-free protein options, market research increasingly shows that the majority of actual purchasers identify as regular meat-eaters who buy plant-based products occasionally alongside, rather than instead of, traditional meat, often citing curiosity or a desire to moderately reduce meat consumption without fully eliminating it. This finding has prompted some plant-based brands to shift marketing language away from messaging aimed at committed vegetarians and toward messaging aimed at meat-eaters interested in variety or moderation, a strategic pivot that several brands report has corresponded with increased sales.
options: Vegetarians and Vegans Confirmed as the Primary Purchasers
Meat-Eaters Found to Show No Interest in Plant-Based Products
The Marketing Pivot Found to Correspond with Decreased Sales
Marketing Pivot Toward Meat-Eaters Matching Plant-Based Products' Real Buyers
quests.correctAnswer: Marketing Pivot Toward Meat-Eaters Matching Plant-Based Products' Real Buyers
quests.hint: Think about who plant-based meat products were originally marketed to and who the research found is actually buying them most.
quests.explanation: The passage shows a mismatch between the original target marketing audience and the actual primary purchasers, leading to a successful marketing pivot, so the summary should capture that realignment between assumption and reality.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Whereas early ride-hailing apps relied on drivers manually accepting or declining individual ride requests as they appeared, some platforms have since introduced batch matching systems that assign drivers to several upcoming rides simultaneously, optimizing routes across multiple passengers rather than offering one ride at a time. While this approach can increase a driver's total earnings per hour by reducing idle time between fares, driver feedback indicates considerable frustration with reduced autonomy over which specific rides they accept, since batch-assigned rides often cannot be individually declined without affecting the entire optimized route, illustrating a tension between system-level efficiency and individual driver control.
options: Batch Matching Confirmed to Increase Driver Autonomy
Manual Ride Acceptance Found to Generate Higher Hourly Earnings
Drivers Found to Welcome the Loss of Individual Ride Choice
Batch Matching Raising Earnings While Reducing Driver Control
quests.correctAnswer: Batch Matching Raising Earnings While Reducing Driver Control
quests.hint: Think about the efficiency benefit batch matching provides and the autonomy cost drivers experience, then notice that the passage frames this as a tension between two competing goods.
quests.explanation: The passage presents a genuine trade-off between system efficiency and individual driver control, so the summary should capture both sides of that tension rather than present the system as purely beneficial or purely harmful.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Although clinical trials for new medications have traditionally required participants to meet narrow eligibility criteria designed to isolate a drug's effect from confounding variables, this practice has meant that trial populations often look considerably healthier and younger than the broader population of patients who will eventually take the approved medication in real-world practice, including many with other coexisting conditions excluded from the original trial. Researchers studying this gap have found that real-world effectiveness and side effect rates sometimes differ meaningfully from trial results, prompting some regulatory agencies to require additional real-world monitoring data after approval rather than relying solely on the original narrow trial population's results.
options: Trial Populations Confirmed to Closely Match Real-World Patients
Narrow Trial Populations Creating a Gap with Real-World Drug Effects
Real-World Effectiveness Found to Always Match Trial Results Exactly
Regulatory Agencies Found to Reject All Post-Approval Monitoring
quests.correctAnswer: Narrow Trial Populations Creating a Gap with Real-World Drug Effects
quests.hint: Think about how narrow trial eligibility criteria might create a mismatch between the people studied and the people who actually take the drug afterward.
quests.explanation: The passage shows that the narrow design of clinical trials, while useful for isolating drug effects, creates a real gap with broader real-world populations, prompting additional monitoring, so the summary should capture that gap and its regulatory response.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Whereas video game difficulty has traditionally been presented as a single adjustable setting chosen once at the start of a game, some developers have begun implementing dynamic difficulty systems that quietly adjust challenge in real time based on a player's recent performance, becoming slightly easier after repeated failures or slightly harder after an unusually smooth streak, without ever notifying the player that an adjustment occurred. Player surveys reveal a notable split: many players report enjoying a smoother, less frustrating experience without realizing why, while others who eventually discover the hidden adjustment feel a sense of betrayal, arguing that invisible difficulty changes undermine a genuine sense of accomplishment.
options: Hidden Difficulty Adjustments Splitting Players Between Comfort and Betrayal
All Players Confirmed to Prefer Dynamic Difficulty Adjustment
Dynamic Systems Found to Always Increase Difficulty Over Time
Players Who Discover the Adjustment Found to Feel Unaffected
quests.correctAnswer: Hidden Difficulty Adjustments Splitting Players Between Comfort and Betrayal
quests.hint: Think about the two different reactions players have to dynamic difficulty, one group unaware and comfortable, another aware and upset, and notice that both reactions exist simultaneously.
quests.explanation: The passage presents a genuine split in player reaction to the same hidden system, so the summary should capture both the positive and negative responses rather than present player reaction as uniform in either direction.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Although wedding invitations have traditionally followed strict formal etiquette rules regarding wording, such as never directly mentioning gift registries on the invitation itself, etiquette consultants note that this convention has increasingly clashed with practical guest expectations, since many guests report frustration at needing to search separately for registry information through word of mouth or a wedding website. Some couples have begun including registry information via a small, clearly optional supplementary card rather than on the formal invitation itself, a compromise that etiquette experts suggest preserves traditional formality on the primary invitation while still meeting practical guest needs through a separate, secondary element.
options: Traditional Etiquette Confirmed to Meet All Guest Expectations
Guests Found to Have No Interest in Registry Information
A Supplementary Card Compromise Balancing Etiquette with Guest Needs
Couples Found to Abandon Formal Invitations Entirely
quests.correctAnswer: A Supplementary Card Compromise Balancing Etiquette with Guest Needs
quests.hint: Think about the tension between traditional etiquette rules and practical guest needs, and what compromise some couples found to address both.
quests.explanation: The passage shows a practical compromise resolving a tension between formal tradition and guest convenience, so the summary should capture that balanced solution rather than describe only the traditional rule or only the guest frustration.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Whereas many people assume that the most efficient way to clean a home is to tackle one room completely before moving to the next, professional organizers increasingly advocate for a task-based approach instead, completing one type of task, such as all dusting, across every room before moving to the next task type, such as all vacuuming, arguing that this method reduces the repeated mental switching between different types of physical motion and tools that room-by-room cleaning requires. Time-tracking comparisons of both methods found the task-based approach completed in less total time for homes with more than four rooms, though the room-by-room method remained comparably fast for smaller homes.
options: Room-by-Room Cleaning Confirmed Faster for All Home Sizes
Task-Based Cleaning Saving Time in Larger Homes, Not Smaller Ones
Task-Based Cleaning Found to Take Longer Regardless of Home Size
Time Differences Between Methods Found to Be Unrelated to Home Size
quests.correctAnswer: Task-Based Cleaning Saving Time in Larger Homes, Not Smaller Ones
quests.hint: Think about the two cleaning methods being compared and notice that the passage specifies the time difference depends on the size of the home.
quests.explanation: The passage shows that the advantage of task-based cleaning depends on home size, helping more in larger homes while making little difference in smaller ones, so the summary should capture that conditional finding rather than declare one method universally faster.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Although classroom seating arrangements have traditionally been organized into rows facing the teacher, based partly on long-standing convention rather than instructional research, some teachers experimenting with flexible seating, including standing desks, floor cushions, and small group clusters that students choose based on their preferred working style for a given task, report mixed results that seem to depend heavily on the specific activity, with flexible arrangements correlating with better engagement during collaborative work but showing no clear advantage, and sometimes a slight disadvantage, during tasks requiring individual, sustained concentration like silent reading.
options: Flexible Seating Confirmed to Improve Every Type of Classroom Task
Traditional Row Seating Found to Improve Collaborative Work Most
Flexible Seating Helping Collaboration but Not Individual Concentration Tasks
Flexible Seating Found to Show No Effect on Any Task Type
quests.correctAnswer: Flexible Seating Helping Collaboration but Not Individual Concentration Tasks
quests.hint: Think about the two different types of classroom tasks the passage compares and notice that flexible seating did not show the same effect for both.
quests.explanation: The passage shows that the benefit of flexible seating depends on the type of task, helping collaborative work while offering no advantage for individual concentration tasks, so the summary should capture that task-dependent nuance rather than treat flexible seating as universally better or worse.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Whereas employee referral programs have traditionally been valued by companies primarily for reducing recruiting costs compared to other hiring channels, longitudinal data tracking employee performance and retention found that referred employees also stayed at their jobs significantly longer on average than employees hired through other channels, even after controlling for role and starting salary, suggesting referral programs may offer a meaningful retention benefit beyond the cost savings companies typically emphasize when promoting these programs internally.
options: Referral Programs Offering a Retention Benefit Beyond Cost Savings
Referral Programs Confirmed to Offer Only Cost Savings
Referred Employees Found to Leave Sooner Than Other Hires
Retention Differences Found to Disappear After Controlling for Role and Salary
quests.correctAnswer: Referral Programs Offering a Retention Benefit Beyond Cost Savings
quests.hint: Think about what companies traditionally emphasize about referral programs and what the retention data revealed about an additional benefit beyond that.
quests.explanation: The passage shows that referral programs provide a meaningful benefit, longer retention, beyond the cost savings companies typically focus on, so the summary should capture that additional, less-emphasized benefit rather than describe only the cost angle.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Although travel itineraries packed with back-to-back activities have traditionally been marketed by tour companies as maximizing the value of a limited vacation, since every available hour is filled with planned activity, surveys of returning travelers found that those who built in substantial unstructured free time alongside planned activities reported higher overall vacation satisfaction than travelers with fully packed schedules, even when the fully packed travelers technically visited more total sites, suggesting that perceived restfulness may contribute as much to vacation satisfaction as the sheer quantity of experiences accumulated.
options: Fully Packed Itineraries Confirmed to Maximize Vacation Satisfaction
Unstructured Time Found to Reduce Overall Vacation Satisfaction
Travelers Who Visited More Sites Found to Report Higher Satisfaction
Unstructured Free Time Boosting Satisfaction Despite Fewer Sites Visited
quests.correctAnswer: Unstructured Free Time Boosting Satisfaction Despite Fewer Sites Visited
quests.hint: Think about the traditional assumption that packing more activities into a trip maximizes value, and what the survey found about travelers who included more free time instead.
quests.explanation: The passage challenges the assumption that more packed activity automatically means more satisfaction, showing that unstructured time contributed meaningfully to satisfaction even with fewer sites visited, so the summary should capture that counterintuitive finding.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Whereas fast food value menus have traditionally been priced as a way to attract budget-conscious customers who might otherwise skip a purchase entirely, some chains have found that value menu items often serve as a gateway purchase that customers later supplement with additional higher-margin items, such as a drink or dessert not included in the original value item, meaning the actual average transaction total for value menu customers frequently approaches that of customers who ordered a standard combo meal from the start. This finding has led some chains to maintain or even expand value menu options rather than treating them purely as a low-margin loss leader.
options: Value Menu Customers Confirmed to Spend Far Less Overall
Value Menu Items Leading to Add-On Purchases That Boost Totals
Chains Found to Eliminate Value Menus After This Discovery
Add-On Purchases Found to Be Unrelated to Value Menu Items
quests.correctAnswer: Value Menu Items Leading to Add-On Purchases That Boost Totals
quests.hint: Think about what chains originally assumed about value menu customers' spending and what the actual transaction data revealed about their total purchases.
quests.explanation: The passage shows that value menu customers often end up spending close to what standard combo customers spend due to add-on purchases, so the summary should capture that surprising similarity rather than assume value menu customers always spend much less.

quests.instruction: Choose the best summary for the paragraph.
quests.passage: Although software updates have traditionally been pushed to users automatically and immediately upon release, on the assumption that the newest version is always the most secure and capable, some organizations managing critical infrastructure have adopted a deliberate delay policy, waiting a set period after a new update's release before installing it organization-wide, allowing time for any newly introduced bugs to surface and be reported by other users first. While this approach means these organizations sometimes lag behind on the latest features, incident reports show meaningfully fewer disruptions caused by buggy updates compared to organizations that install every update immediately upon release.

Organizations Delaying Updates Found to Experience More Bugs
Delayed Update Installation Reducing Disruptions from Buggy Releases

quests.hint: Think about the trade-off the passage describes between getting the newest features immediately and waiting to see if problems are reported by other users first.
